previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with mitochondrial disease, autonomic dysfunction, coronary artery disease, and hypogammaglobulinemia was admitted for observation during a scheduled biweekly IVIG infusion. He reported a brief episode of near-syncope at home triggered by cold exposure, but was asymptomatic on admission. The IVIG infusion was administered with premedication and IV fluids. During the infusion, he developed mild chest tightness, shortness of breath, and hand tingling, which improved with oxygen and slowing the infusion rate. Symptoms resolved post-infusion, and he remained hemodynamically stable without hypoxia or arrhythmias. He was monitored on telemetry and observed overnight. No medication changes were made. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans to continue outpatient IVIG and follow-up with specialists.
